registered: 2026-11-07, before any solo label exists and before the model was run on the evaluation sample
purpose: Decide whether the pinned pretrained SMS model stays the EXPERIMENTAL evidence source for the three-day MVP, from one reviewer's labels on a small blinded sample. This never validates the model: a solo sample cannot replace the independent two-reviewer plus adjudicator label-approval gate (95% Wilson lower bound, cluster-weighted), which is unchanged and still BLOCKED.
change_rule: These numbers may be changed only before the first label is written. The evaluation recomputes this file's SHA-256 and refuses to run if it differs from the copy recorded when the sample was prepared.
mapping_note: A comparison mapping, not a calibration. The model's `fraud` label covers phishing and scams (its card), so both human scam labels count as fraud. `unclear` and blank rows are excluded from every matrix and counted separately.
primary_input: The same masked display text the reviewer saw. The raw stored text is scored too and reported as a secondary table; it never decides the verdict.
pools: Collected and synthetic data are never pooled. The verdict uses the collected pool; the synthetic pool (false alarms on legitimate transactional and OTP wording) can only lower it.

completeness.below_min: INCOMPLETE: no verdict, nothing is scored

minimum_denominators_collected.below_min: capped at CONDITIONAL, with the short class named

go.meaning: Keep the model as clearly labelled experimental evidence and carry it into the M4.3 comparison. Not validated, not calibrated, not production.

no_go.meaning: Do not present this model's output as a fraud indicator in the MVP. Fall back to the unavailable state and the TF-IDF baseline plan.

conditional.meaning: Neither GO nor NO-GO: use only as experimental evidence with the named shortfalls stated next to it, and collect more labels before relying on it.
conditional.applies_when: No NO-GO rule fires, and any GO rule fails or a cap applies.

interval: Wilson score interval, 95%. Rates are one-versus-rest on the mapped classes. The unit is one message per campaign cluster, so rates are not prevalence estimates.
reviewer_repeat_agreement: The sheet re-presents a few messages under new item IDs. Agreement is the share of such pairs where both labels exist and match. Fewer than 5 usable pairs counts as not met (cap at CONDITIONAL).
not_claimed: performance on live traffic, other languages, or other scam types
